recommendations.text: The poisoned patient requires simultaneous stabilization and toxin identification. ABCs take priority. Key labs: acetaminophen and salicylate levels in all intentional ingestions. Ipecac is no longer recommended.

For Toxicological Emergency Stabilization, the following actions are mandatory: - assess airway breathing circulation (within 2 minutes) - assess vital signs (within 5 minutes) - obtain exposure history (within 15 minutes) - assess toxidrome
During Toxicological Emergency Stabilization, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: induce emesis, give ipecac, delay resuscitation.

Toxidrome recognition guides empiric management: sympathomimetic, anticholinergic, cholinergic, opioid, sedative-hypnotic. ECG is essential - QRS >100ms suggests sodium channel blockade (TCAs), QTc prolongation suggests multiple agents.
For Toxin Identification and Classification, the following actions are mandatory: - identify toxin class (within 30 minutes) - review ecg for toxicity (within 15 minutes)

Converted from unconditional: when clinical toxidrome strongly suggests a specific toxin, empiric antidote should not be delayed for confirmatory testing [FORBIDDEN: delay_empiric_antidote_if_indicated] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 2; empiric antidote should not be withheld pending identification

recommendations.text: Forced diuresis for toxin clearance is ineffective and causes dangerous fluid overload and electrolyte imbalances. [FORBIDDEN: give_forced_diuresis_in_poisoning, give_mannitol_for_toxin_clearance] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 5; forced diuresis is ineffective and causes pulmonary edema and electrolyte derangement

recommendations.text: Specific antidotes should be administered as soon as the toxin is identified or strongly suspected. NAC for acetaminophen, naloxone for opioids, digoxin Fab for digoxin, fomepizole for toxic alcohols.
For Toxin-Specific Antidote Administration, the following actions are mandatory: - administer specific antidote (within 30 minutes)

Converted from unconditional: antidote delay worsens outcomes for all identified toxins; NAC efficacy drops after 8h, naloxone delay causes anoxic brain injury [FORBIDDEN: delay_antidote] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3; antidote delay increases morbidity and mortality

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: activated charcoal after endoscopy obscures mucosal visualization and interferes with subsequent endoscopic assessment [FORBIDDEN: give_charcoal_after_endoscopy] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 4; charcoal after endoscopy impairs visualization

recommendations.text: NAC is nearly 100% effective if given within 8 hours of acetaminophen ingestion; prevents hepatotoxicity by replenishing glutathione. Always indicated above Rumack-Matthew treatment line. [REQUIRED: give_n_acetylcysteine] (Severity: CRITICAL)

In acetaminophen overdose, hepatotoxic agents worsen liver injury and NAC delay beyond 8h drops efficacy dramatically. [FORBIDDEN: give_hepatotoxic_drug_in_apap_overdose, delay_nac_for_level_confirmation] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.1; NAC must not be delayed waiting for acetaminophen level; additional hepatotoxins compound liver injury

recommendations.text: Flumazenil in chronic benzodiazepine users precipitates refractory seizures and death by acute GABA withdrawal; supportive care with airway management is preferred. [FORBIDDEN: give_flumazenil] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.2; Haverkos GP, Clin Pharm 1994

recommendations.text: Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression; start low (0.04-0.4 mg) and titrate to respiratory effort to avoid precipitating withdrawal. [REQUIRED: give_naloxone] (Severity: CRITICAL)

In opioid overdose, additional opioids or long-acting sedatives worsen respiratory depression and may cause fatal apnea. [FORBIDDEN: give_additional_opioid_in_overdose, give_long_acting_sedative_in_opioid_od] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.3; Boyer EW, NEJM 2012; additional CNS depressants worsen respiratory depression

recommendations.text: Physostigmine in TCA overdose causes refractory seizures, bradycardia, and asystole; it reverses anticholinergic effects but worsens cardiac sodium channel blockade. [FORBIDDEN: give_physostigmine] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.4; Pentel P, Ann Emerg Med 1980

recommendations.text: QRS >100ms in TCA overdose indicates significant sodium channel blockade with seizure and arrhythmia risk; sodium bicarbonate overcomes blockade and alkalinizes to reduce free drug. [REQUIRED: give_sodium_bicarbonate] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.4; Liebelt EL, J Toxicol Clin Toxicol 1995

recommendations.text: Fomepizole inhibits alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing conversion of methanol/ethylene glycol to toxic metabolites (formic acid/oxalic acid). Must be given before metabolic acidosis develops. [REQUIRED: give_fomepizole] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Delaying fomepizole for osmolar gap results permits conversion to formic acid/oxalic acid; concurrent ethanol adds toxicity. [FORBIDDEN: delay_fomepizole_for_osmolar_gap, give_ethanol_concurrently_with_fomepizole] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.5; Brent J, NEJM 2001; fomepizole delay allows toxic metabolite accumulation

recommendations.text: Digoxin-specific Fab fragments bind free digoxin; indicated for life-threatening arrhythmias, hyperkalemia >5.5, or digoxin level >6 ng/mL. [REQUIRED: give_digoxin_fab_fragments] (Severity: CRITICAL)

IV calcium in digoxin toxicity causes fatal myocardial contracture; cardioversion without Fab triggers lethal arrhythmia. [FORBIDDEN: give_calcium_in_digoxin_toxicity, cardiovert_without_digoxin_fab] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.6; Antman EM, Circulation 1990; calcium + digoxin causes 'stone heart' (irreversible contracture)

recommendations.text: Organophosphate poisoning requires atropine (titrated to drying of secretions) plus pralidoxime (reactivates acetylcholinesterase before aging occurs, ideally within 24-48h). [REQUIRED: give_atropine, give_pralidoxime] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Succinylcholine relies on pseudocholinesterase for metabolism; OP poisoning inhibits this enzyme causing prolonged paralysis. [FORBIDDEN: give_succinylcholine_in_op_poisoning, give_morphine_in_cholinergic_crisis] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.7; Eddleston M, Lancet 2008; OP inhibits pseudocholinesterase causing prolonged paralysis from succinylcholine

recommendations.text: Glucagon bypasses beta-receptor blockade by directly activating adenylate cyclase; give 5-10 mg IV bolus then 1-5 mg/h infusion for refractory bradycardia and hypotension. [REQUIRED: give_glucagon_high_dose] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.8; Love JN, J Toxicol Clin Toxicol 2000

recommendations.text: Additional beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers in beta-blocker overdose cause refractory cardiogenic shock. [FORBIDDEN: give_additional_beta_blocker, give_verapamil_in_beta_blocker_od] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.8; Love JN, J Toxicol Clin Toxicol 2000; additional negative chronotropes cause refractory bradycardia

recommendations.text: High-dose insulin euglycemia therapy (1-10 U/kg/h) improves cardiac output in CCB overdose; calcium provides temporary inotropic support. [REQUIRED: give_high_dose_insulin_euglycemia, give_calcium_chloride] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.9; Engebretsen KM, Clin Toxicol 2011

recommendations.text: Beta-blockers in CCB overdose compound negative inotropy and vasodilation causing irreversible cardiogenic shock. [FORBIDDEN: give_additional_ccb, give_beta_blocker_in_ccb_overdose] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT/ACMT 2024 Section 3.9; Engebretsen KM, Clin Toxicol 2011; combined negative inotropy is lethal

recommendations.text: Single-dose activated charcoal (1 g/kg) should be considered if <1-2 hours post-ingestion and airway is protected. Contraindicated with caustics, hydrocarbons, or unprotected airway. Ipecac is no longer recommended.
For Gastrointestinal Decontamination, the following actions are mandatory: - assess decontamination indication (within 30 minutes)
During Gastrointestinal Decontamination, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give activated charcoal if unprotected airway.
Activated charcoal contraindicated in caustic ingestion - risk of perforation. [FORBIDDEN: give_activated_charcoal_with_caustic, give_activated_charcoal] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT Position Statement; Hojer J, Clin Toxicol 2013

recommendations.text: Charcoal with hydrocarbons increases aspiration risk. [FORBIDDEN: give_activated_charcoal_with_hydrocarbon, give_activated_charcoal] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT Position Statement; Isbister GK, Med J Aust 2004

recommendations.text: Whole bowel irrigation contraindicated in bowel obstruction. [FORBIDDEN: give_whole_bowel_irrigation_with_obstruction] (Severity: HIGH)

Supportive care is the foundation of toxicological management. Benzodiazepines are first-line for toxicologic seizures (phenytoin is contraindicated). External cooling, not antipyretics, for toxicologic hyperthermia.
For Supportive Care, the following actions are mandatory: - provide supportive care (within 30 minutes) - reassess clinical status
During Supportive Care, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give antipyretic for hyperthermia toxicologic, physically restrain without sedation.
Forced diuresis is obsolete except in specific cases (rhabdomyolysis). [FORBIDDEN: give_forced_diuresis] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AACT Guidelines; Shannon MW, Clin Toxicol 2007

recommendations.text: Observation duration depends on toxin kinetics: 4-6 hours for immediate-release, 12-24 hours for sustained-release. All intentional ingestions require psychiatric evaluation before discharge.
For Monitoring and Disposition, the following actions are mandatory: - serial vital sign monitoring (within 60 minutes) - serial lab monitoring - determine disposition (within 360 minutes)

During Monitoring and Disposition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without psychiatry evaluation, discharge during absorption phase, discharge without observation period.
